purpose: Guarantee that crates/binding, the workspace's only NAPI/FFI boundary, never lets a Rust panic reach the host Node.js process - every entry point either delegates directly to crates/core or fails with a catchable JS Error - and that concurrently created watch sessions never collide.
scope: The five #[napi] entry points in crates/binding/src/lib.rs: extract_all, create_session, initialize_session, extract_file_incremental, close_session
The panic_guard::contain_panic wrapping around each entry point's core session/pipeline call, per ADR-0005
The next_session_id() ID-generation scheme and its collision behavior under concurrent session creation
The delegation boundary between crates/binding and caliper_docgen_core::pipeline / WatchSession, including auto-vivification of a WatchSession for an unrecognized caller-supplied session_id
non_goals: The extraction/resolution logic itself, owned by crates/core (pipeline::extract, WatchSession internals)
The JS-side wrapper package's API surface outside this Rust workspace
Widening the session-ID counter beyond its current 16-bit allocation, or adding collision-detection retry logic - the wrap-after-65536-allocations gap is an accepted, documented tradeoff per ADR-0005

PipelineOptions field validation/parsing correctness (TryFrom<JsExtractOptions>) -- a separate input-validation concern from this spec's panic-safety and delegation focus. Not required to be inside the contain_panic guard by this spec, though an implementation may choose to include it (as create_session, initialize_session, and extract_file_incremental currently do; extract_all currently does not).

Whether a panic caught inside close_session's closure is surfaced as a structured Diagnostic/log event before being discarded -- current implementation discards it via `let _ = contain_panic(...)`; accepted gap relative to CLAUDE.md's Diagnostic non-negotiable, not fixed by this spec

Race behavior when two concurrent calls to extract_file_incremental/initialize_session supply the same never-before-seen session_id (last-write-wins on SESSIONS.insert, discarding whichever WatchSession lost the race) -- accepted low-severity gap distinct from the next_session_id() generation-collision guarantee AC4 covers

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each of the five #[napi] functions wraps its core panic-risk work inside a single caliper_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic call: for extract_all, pipeline::extract(...) AND the subsequent JSON serialization of its result (extraction_output_to_json); for create_session, the next_session_id()+WatchSession::new(...)+SESSIONS.insert(...) sequence; for initialize_session and extract_file_incremental, BOTH the session lookup-or-auto-vivify sequence (SESSIONS.get, and when absent, WatchSession::new(...)+SESSIONS.insert(...)) AND the function's existing core call (session.initialize() / session.update_file(...) respectively); for close_session, SESSIONS.remove(...). Argument deserialization performed by the #[napi] macro, and the PipelineOptions::try_from(options) conversion, are not required to be inside the guard. Confirmable by reading the source and locating, for each of the five functions, a single contain_panic(...) call whose closure body contains every named operation for that function.

A panic triggered inside create_session's wrapped closure (via CREATE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL) is caught by contain_panic and returned to the caller as napi::Result::Err, not an unwind crossing the FFI boundary -- verifiable by calling create_session with the sentinel src_dir and asserting Err is returned rather than the test process aborting.

A panic triggered inside close_session's wrapped closure -- via a CLOSE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL: u32 reserved session_id value, checked inside the contain_panic closure body under #[cfg(test)], mirroring CREATE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL's pattern -- is caught by contain_panic and close_session returns normally (unit type) without the panic propagating to the caller or crashing the host process -- verifiable by calling close_session(CLOSE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL) and asserting the call completes without the test process aborting.

next_session_id() combines the low 16 bits of the OS process ID with a per-process monotonic counter (also masked to 16 bits) such that two sessions created concurrently within the same process cannot receive the same generated ID until more than 65,536 create_session calls have occurred in that process's lifetime -- verifiable by reading next_session_id()'s implementation and confirming the bit-packing formula, and by a test that calls it N times within one process and asserts no duplicate IDs for N <= 65,536.

crates/binding/src/lib.rs contains no component-extraction or type-resolution logic of its own: extract_all's real work is a call to caliper_docgen_core::pipeline::extract followed by JSON serialization of its result, create_session/initialize_session/extract_file_incremental's real work is construction of or a call into caliper_docgen_core::pipeline::WatchSession, and close_session's real work is a SESSIONS.remove call -- confirmable by reading the crate's source for the absence of AST traversal, prop extraction, or type-resolution code.

A panic triggered inside extract_all's wrapped closure (via an EXTRACT_ALL_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL added to JsExtractOptions.src_dirs, mirroring the CREATE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL pattern) is caught by contain_panic and the returned Future resolves to napi::Result::Err rather than the spawn_blocking task aborting -- verifiable by awaiting extract_all with the sentinel option and asserting Err is returned rather than the test process aborting. The sentinel may trigger the panic at either the pipeline::extract(...) step or the subsequent JSON-serialization step named in AC1 -- both are required to be inside the guard, and either triggering point satisfies this criterion.

A panic triggered inside initialize_session's wrapped closure -- via an INITIALIZE_SESSION_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL: u32 reserved session_id value, checked inside the contain_panic closure body under #[cfg(test)] (the closure captures session_id for this purpose) -- is caught by contain_panic and the returned Future resolves to napi::Result::Err rather than the spawn_blocking task aborting -- verifiable by awaiting initialize_session with the sentinel session_id and any valid options, and asserting Err is returned rather than the test process aborting. The sentinel check is placed at the point of the existing core call (session.initialize()), after the lookup-or-auto-vivify sequence has completed for a normally-registered session_id -- distinct from AC10's construction-time trigger, which fires during auto-vivified WatchSession construction instead.

A panic triggered inside extract_file_incremental's wrapped closure (via an EXTRACT_FILE_INCREMENTAL_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL file_path, mirroring the same pattern) is caught by contain_panic and the returned Future resolves to napi::Result::Err rather than the spawn_blocking task aborting -- verifiable the same way as AC6. The sentinel check is placed at the point of the existing core call (session.update_file(...)), after the lookup-or-auto-vivify sequence has completed for a normally-registered session_id -- distinct from AC10's construction-time trigger, which fires during auto-vivified WatchSession construction instead.

extract_file_incremental and initialize_session, when called with a session_id not present in SESSIONS, do not return an error solely on that basis: each constructs a new WatchSession from the call's PipelineOptions and inserts it into SESSIONS under the supplied session_id before proceeding, such that the call succeeds as if a prior create_session() call had generated this session_id and inserted its session into SESSIONS. This is not an error case: an unrecognized session_id is valid input that triggers auto-vivification rather than failure -- verifiable by calling either function with a session_id that was never returned by create_session and confirming (a) the call returns Ok, and (b) a subsequent call with the same session_id finds an existing entry in SESSIONS rather than constructing another one.

A panic triggered during auto-vivified WatchSession construction inside initialize_session's or extract_file_incremental's wrapped closure -- via an AUTO_VIVIFY_PANIC_TEST_SENTINEL: u32 reserved session_id value, checked inside the contain_panic closure body before/during WatchSession::new when session_id is not present in SESSIONS -- is caught by contain_panic and the returned Future resolves to napi::Result::Err rather than the spawn_blocking task aborting -- verifiable by awaiting either function with the sentinel session_id (never previously registered via create_session) and asserting Err is returned rather than the test process aborting.

close_session with a session_id absent from SESSIONS (never created, or already closed by a prior close_session call) returns normally (no error, no panic) -- SESSIONS.remove's Option<_> result is discarded regardless of whether an entry existed. Verifiable by calling close_session once with a session_id that was never issued by create_session, and by calling close_session twice in succession with the same valid, previously-created session_id, asserting all three calls return without error.
